name: Kistefos
funding: Christen Sveaas, his investment company Kistefos AS and Christen Sveaas' art foundation; Riksantikvaren, local and county councils and savings-bank foundations.
watch: Sculpture park and museum in Jevnaker featuring 'The Twist' by BIG.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2010 to 2025 with full accounts and names funders; the site names only the board chair, the register the rest.

name: Kamloops Art Gallery
funding: City of Kamloops, Province of BC, BC Arts Council, Canada Council, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Audain and Hamber foundations. BC Lottery Corporation sponsors free Thursday admission.
watch: BCLC is a provincial Crown corporation. The Cullen Commission (2022) found it ignored police warnings about casino money laundering until 2015.
records_note: Posts its 2025 annual report and signed 2025 financial statements, names donors in tiers since January 2024, and lists its trustees in the report.

name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Municipal, run by the Kanazawa Art Promotion Foundation.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Attendance widely reported above 1M a year; roster not checked.
why_flagged: Gold member Kanazawa Energy is a city-gas utility, 48% Hokuriku Electric and 43% Toho Gas. Iwatani Central Hokuriku (LPG) also listed. No protest found.
records_note: Kanazawa 21 posts its 2025 annual report and names its supporting members by tier undated, but publishes no accounts or board.

name: ILHAM Gallery
funding: No funder list is published. Yayasan ILHAM, a nonprofit, has run it since 2019; IB Tower Sdn Bhd ran it from 2015. Ilham Tower is owned via Daim family firms.
watch: Public art gallery in Kuala Lumpur committed to Southeast Asian contemporary art.
records_note: Yayasan ILHAM, the non-profit that runs it, posts no reports, accounts, funders or board; its About pages name staff only.

name: Charleston
funding: Charity running Charleston farmhouse and its Wolfson Gallery. Gifts and grants from the Art Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund and Arts Council England; Bloomberg Connects supplies its digital guide.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies runs Bloomberg Connects. More than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Charleston was not named.
records_note: One annual report found (2023), accounts on the Charity Commission register, no standing funder list, and trustees named on the Team page.

name: Museo de Arte de Lima
funding: 2023: half from courses, a quarter Patronato members, a quarter events/tickets; about 150k visits; allies Fundación Telefónica, ICPNA.
watch: Camisea, operated by Pluspetrol, sponsored free Thursday entry from August 2022 to March 2025. Alberto Rebaza chairs the board.
why_flagged: KPMG-audited 2025 revenue S/17.1M: tuition 38%, donations and memberships 37%, services 25%. Donors named: Fundación Telefónica, JOMA, THOMA, Smurfit Kappa. Camisea gas consortium funded free Thursdays.
records_note: Posts audited accounts for 2003 to 2025, committee annual reports for 2007 to 2021 and a named board; its partners page shows an unnamed banner.

name: Lismore Castle Arts
funding: Not-for-profit initiative founded 2005. Exhibitions are funded by the Arts Council and the Waterford City & County Council Arts Grant; an older page also lists the Henry Moore Foundation.
watch: Non-profit contemporary exhibition space in County Waterford.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or board; the about page credits the Arts Council and the Waterford City and County Council arts grant, undated.

name: Mostyn
funding: £0.7M income (FY2026). Arts Council of Wales £385k, Conwy County Borough Council, Llandudno Town Council, National Gallery; Garfield Weston, Henry Moore, Ampersand, Foyle, Ashley Foundation, Mostyn Estates.
watch: Registered Welsh charity dedicated to contemporary visual art.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the support page names partners and donors undated, and trustees are not listed.

name: Camden Art Centre
funding: Arts Council England, DCMS, Bloomberg Philanthropies (programme support), trusts including AKO, Foyle, Freelands and Henry Moore, and patrons including Batia and Idan Ofer.
watch: Bloomberg title-sponsors New Contemporaries since 2001. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Camden was not named.
why_flagged: Bloomberg title-sponsors New Contemporaries since 2001. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Camden was not named.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the thank-you page names funders and patrons undated, and no trustees are listed.

name: Chisenhale Gallery
funding: £1.0M income (FY2025). Arts Council England 17%; Bloomberg Philanthropies £120k digital grant (2024); Ford, Terra, Asymmetry, Freelands and Mondriaan funds; Friends and Patrons circles.
why_flagged: Name to know: Bloomberg Philanthropies, which faces a May 2026 UK artists' letter to London theatres; not aimed at Chisenhale. Fondation Pernod Ricard also gives.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, a Funders and Partners page names funders for 2023-24, and trustees are listed.

name: Gasworks
funding: £1.0M income (FY2026). Arts Council England £290k, City Bridge Foundation, Lambeth, British Council, Cockayne fund, Great Britain Sasakawa Foundation, Henry Moore Foundation, residency trusts and patrons.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Thank You page names funders undated, and nine trustees are listed.

name: Sir John Soane's Museum
funding: £4.2M income (2024-25). DCMS grant-in-aid £1.165M; trusts and patrons including Linbury, Leverhulme, Wates, Deborah Loeb Brice Foundation; brand licensing partners.
watch: Non-Departmental Public Body established by an 1833 Act of Parliament. Transparent audited accounts submitted annually to Parliament.
records_note: Annual reports with accounts from 2011-12 to 2024-25 on its site, donors named in the 2024-25 report, and trustees listed.
